metadata.title: Remainders Are Structural
metadata.description: Connect quotient-remainder structure with factorial notation and modular reasoning.

content.text: The division algorithm is Dividend = Divisor×Quotient + Remainder. When a process is reversed, rebuild the number from the quotient and remainder rather than performing division again.
Factorials are products from 1 through n, with 0!=1. For modular questions, discard every component known to be divisible by the modulus and keep only the surviving remainder.
Let's start with the quotient-remainder identity.
For multi-step transformations, work backward from the stated final value. It often removes variables and makes the route nearly mechanical.
Now simplify factorial expressions by factoring out a common factorial.
Finish with a factorial sum modulo 5.
Good. You now have a clean way to move between division structure, factorials, and remainders.
